source_text:
In sanctum Lucam (homilia 21) [Dub.]
̔Ησυχίου, πρεσβυτέρου Ἱεροσολύμων, ἐγκώμιον εἰς τὸν ἅγιον Λουκᾶν
τὸν ἀπόστολον καὶ εὐαγγελιστήν.
1 Φόβῳ τοῦ σιωπᾶν μὴ ἀνεχόμενος περὶ τῆς παρούσης ἑορτῆς, εἰ καὶ λίαν εἰμὶ
ἀμαθὴς τῷ λόγῳ ὁ τάλας ἐγὼ καὶ οὐκ ἀξίως ἔχων τοῦ λέγειν, ὅμως τῷ πόθῳ
ἑλκόμενος τὸ χρέος κατὰ δύναμιν ἀπο δίδωμι. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ καὶ λόγων καὶ ἔργων
ἅμιλλαν ὁρῶ ἐπὶ τῆς παρούσης πανηγύρεως, τῶν μὲν λόγων βιαζομένων
παραστῆσαι τῶν ἔργων τὸ μέγεθος, τῶν δὲ ἔργων πάλιν φιλονεικούντων δι' ὑπερ
βολὴν θαυμάτων νικῆσαι τῶν λόγων τὸ τάχος, ὅμως νίκην μᾶλλον βελτίω τὴν
τοιαύτην ἡγοῦμαι, εἰ φανείην εἰς ἐπαίνους ἡττώμενος τοῦ μακαρίου Λουκᾶ, ὃς εἰς
διδασκαλίαν καὶ θαύματα πᾶσαν τὴν ἐν οὐρανοῖς καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς κτίσιν ἐνίκησεν.
2 Τί γὰρ εὐαγγελιστοῦ μεῖζον; Τί δὲ τῆς χάριτος ἐκείνου ἴσον, ὃς τῷ λογισμῷ
πᾶσαν τὴν αἰσθητὴν κίνησιν ὑπερβαίνει, ὃς τῇ γλώττῃ τοὺς πατρικοὺς κόλπους
ἠρεύνησεν, ὃς γέγονεν τοῦ ἀπορ ρήτου μυστηρίου βροντή; Ἄνθρωπος ὢν τρίπηχυς,
πηλῷ συμ πεπλεγμένος, πάθεσι πυκτεύων, ὑποκείμενος νόσοις, συγκεκλη ρωμένος
θανάτῳ, εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνέβη τοῖς λογισμοῖς, εἶδε τῇ πίστει τὴν ἄναρχον γέννησιν,
ἐθεάσατο τὸν Λόγον ἐκ πατρικῶν κόλπων ἀπαθῶς προελθόντα καὶ θεὸν ἐκ θεοῦ
γεννηθέντα καὶ εἰς δύο θεοὺς τὴν ἄκτιστον οὐσίαν μὴ μερισθεῖσαν, εἶδε τὴν ἐπὶ
θρόνου ὁμοούσιον τριάδα προσκυνουμένην, ἐν ὑποστάσεσι διῃ ρημένην καὶ φύσει
ἡνωμένην, οὔτε τῆς τριάδος εἰς ἓν πρόσωπον συγκεκλεισμένης, οὔτε τῆς οὐσίας εἰς
ἀριθμὸν ἐκτεινομένης. Καὶ τῶν σεραφὶμ ηὑρέθη τολμηρότερος ὁ εὐαγγελιστής·
ἐκεῖνα μὲν γὰρ διὰ τὴν ἀστραπὴν τὴν ὄψιν καλύπτει, οὗτος δὲ διὰ τὴν χάριν τὴν
γέννησιν ἐθεολόγησεν.
3 Πάλιν δὲ οὐρανόθεν εἰς γῆν καταβὰς καὶ ἐγκύψας τῷ φρικτῷ σπηλαίῳ, τοῖς
τῆς πίστεως ὄμμασιν εἶδε μυστήριον θεοῦ τροπῆς καὶ ἀλλοιώσεως ἀνώτερον, εἶδε
παρθένον ἀνύμφευτον μητέρα, εἶδε γαστέρα οὐρανοῦ πλατυτέραν, εἶδε τόκον οὐκ
ἀρχὴν θεοῦ ἀλλ' ἐπιφάνειαν, εἶδε βρέφος σαρκωθέντα τὸν δημιουργὸν πάν των τῶν
αἰώνων, εἶδε θεὸν ἐν δούλου μορφῇ κενωθέντα, εἶδε φάτνην μυστηρίου κλίνην, εἶδε
σπάργανα οἰκουμένης λύτρα, εἶδε σταυρὸν εἰς οὐρανὸν γέφυραν, εἶδε τάφον κατὰ
θανάτου ὅπ λον, εἶδε Πνεύματος ἁγίου πλοῦτον αἰώνιον καὶ ἀπερινόητον, εἶδεν εἰς
Αἴγυπτον φυγόντα σαρκὶ τὸν κατέχοντα τὴν γῆν δρακί. Καὶ τὸ μὲν μυστήριον ἔλαθε
τὰ σεραφίμ, ὁ δὲ εὐαγγελιστὴς τὸ θαῦμα ἐθεολόγησεν· διὰ τοῦτο Παῦλος, τῶν
εὐαγγελιστῶν τὸ ἀξίωμα κηρύττων, ἐβόα· «ἵνα γνωρισθῇ νῦν ταῖς ἀρχαῖς καὶ ταῖς
thought_title: Luke beholds heaven and the cave
orientation: Hesychius opens the homily by confessing inadequacy yet speaking from love for the feast.
pass_a_gloss: Not enduring from fear to keep silent about the present feast, although I wretched that I am am very unlearned in speech and not having worthily the power to speak, yet drawn by longing I pay the debt according to power. Since I see a rivalry of words and deeds at the present feast, the words straining to set forth the greatness of the deeds, and the deeds again eagerly striving through excess of wonders to conquer the speed of the words, yet I consider such a defeat rather better, if I should appear being defeated in praises by blessed Luke, who in teaching and wonders conquered all creation in heaven and on earth. For what is greater than an evangelist. And what is equal to his grace, who with his mind passed beyond every perceptible motion, who with his tongue searched the fatherly bosoms, who became a thunder of the unutterable mystery. Being a man of three cubits, entangled with mud, boxing with passions, subject to diseases, summoned for death, he went up into heaven with his thoughts, he saw with faith the beginningless generation, he beheld the divine Word coming forth without suffering from fatherly bosoms and God born from God and the uncreated essence not divided into two gods, he saw the Trinity of one essence worshiped on the throne, divided in persons and united in nature, neither the Trinity shut together into one person, nor the essence stretched out into number. And the evangelist was found bolder than the seraphim. For those cover the face because of the lightning, but he through grace spoke as a theologian about the generation. And again coming down from heaven to earth and stooping over the fearful cave, with the eyes of faith he saw a mystery higher than turning and change of God, he saw the Virgin Mary as unwedded mother, he saw a womb broader than heaven, he saw a birth not a beginning of God but a manifestation, he saw the maker of all ages made flesh as an infant, he saw God having emptied himself in a servants form, he saw a manger as a bed of mystery, he saw swaddling clothes as ransom of the inhabited world, he saw a cross as a bridge into heaven, he saw a tomb as a weapon against death, he saw eternal and unthinkable wealth of Holy Spirit, he saw him who holds the earth in the hollow of the hand fleeing into Egypt in flesh. And the mystery escaped the seraphim, but the evangelist spoke as a theologian about the wonder. For this reason Paul, proclaiming the dignity of the evangelists, cried out, in order that now might be made known to the rulers and to the.

choices.why: glossary requires generation for γέννησις; ἄναρχον marks eternal begetting seen by faith, not temporal birth

choices.english: a thunder of the unutterable mystery
choices.why: keeps genitive force and glossary mystery; Luke becomes voice proclaiming what cannot be spoken
literal comparative of size for the virginal conception, not symbolic widening

choices.english: him who holds the earth in the hollow of the hand
choices.why: present participle as substantive subject of fleeing; δραξ is the hand hollow holding earth

bible_refs.note: ἵνα γνωρισθῇ νῦν ταῖς ἀρχαῖς καὶ ταῖς

pass_b_english: Out of fear, I cannot bear to keep silent about this feast. I am wretched and unskilled in speech, and I am unworthy to speak, yet love draws me to pay what I owe as best I can. I see words and deeds competing at this feast. Words strain to display the greatness of deeds, and deeds in turn vie to outrun words by the abundance of wonders. Yet I count it the better victory to be defeated in praising blessed Luke, who in teaching and wonders surpassed every creature in heaven and on earth.

For what is greater than an evangelist? What equals his grace? In his mind he passed beyond every movement of the senses. With his tongue he searched the depths of the Father's heart. He became a thunder of the unutterable mystery.

He was a man only three cubits tall, bound up with clay, wrestling with the passions, subject to sickness, and destined for death. Yet in his thoughts he went up to heaven. By faith he saw the beginningless generation. He beheld the divine Word coming forth impassibly from the Father's heart, God born of God, while the uncreated essence was not divided into two gods. He saw the Trinity, of one essence, worshiped upon the throne, divided among persons and united in nature. The Trinity was not closed up into one person, nor was the essence stretched out into a number. So the evangelist proved bolder than the seraphim. They cover their faces because of the lightning, but by grace he proclaimed the generation.

Then he came down from heaven to earth and bent over the fearful cave. With the eyes of faith he saw a mystery of God beyond change and alteration. He saw the Virgin Mary, an unwedded mother. He saw a womb broader than heaven. He saw a birth that was not the beginning of God but his appearing. He saw the Maker of all ages as an infant made flesh. He saw God self-emptied in the form of a servant. He saw a manger as the bed of the mystery. He saw swaddling clothes as the ransom of the world. He saw the cross as a bridge to heaven. He saw the tomb as a weapon against death. He saw the eternal and unfathomable wealth of the Holy Spirit. He saw him who holds the earth in the hollow of the hand fleeing to Egypt in the flesh. The mystery escaped the seraphim, but the evangelist proclaimed the wonder. And so Paul cries out to proclaim the dignity of the evangelists: "that now it might be made known to the rulers and authorities" (Ephesians 3:10).
notes: Quotation at end breaks off at ταῖς and continues beyond this section; gloss gives only what is present.
Spaced splits like ἀπορ ρήτου, συγκεκλη ρωμένος, ὅπ λον and final δρακί read as line break artifacts, not separate words.

problems.quote: I cannot bear to keep silent about this feast.
problems.source_quote: Φόβῳ τοῦ σιωπᾶν μὴ ἀνεχόμενος περὶ τῆς παρούσης ἑορτῆς,
problems.why: Omits Φόβῳ ('out of fear'), which gives the speaker's motive for speaking and balances 'love' in the next sentence.
problems.fix: Out of fear, I cannot bear to keep silent about this feast.
problems.ruling: Source Φόβῳ τοῦ σιωπᾶν states fear of silence; English drops it and the fear–πόθῳ motive pair.

problems.why: In patristic Greek, πάθεσι here means human passions/desires, not 'sufferings' (sickness and death are listed separately).
problems.ruling: πάθεσι beside νόσοις and θανάτῳ means passions; not sufferings—distinct human limits are merged.

problems.quote: coming forth without suffering from the Father's heart
problems.why: In Trinitarian theology, ἀπαθῶς means 'impassibly / without passion' (unlike human begetting), not 'without suffering.'
problems.fix: coming forth impassibly from the Father's heart
problems.ruling: ἀπαθῶς on the Word from πατρικῶν κόλπων is impassible divine generation, not without suffering/pain.

fixed: Added motive `Out of fear' for Φόβῳ - real omission.
Changed `sufferings' to `the passions' for πάθεσι πυκτεύων, distinct from sickness - real mistranslation.
Changed `without suffering' to `impassibly' for ἀπαθῶς - real mistranslation.
